correctness.rationale: The specified 2(n−1)-vertex canonical root polytope has exposure event equal to the maximum of n−1 absolute Gaussian increments; orientation divides the probability by two. Adding the closing edge gives exact cyclic symmetry 1/n and the positive rare pair event. Conditional correlation −1/2 gives a(t)=Q(t/sqrt3)+Q(sqrt3*t). One-dependent Poisson approximation applies to the separated interior edges because adjacent double exceedances are O(exp(−2t²/3)) and n times that quantity vanishes at the extreme threshold. Gaussian regression under the rare closing-edge condition forces both exceptional neighbors to only one third of the threshold asymptotically. Mills ratios, a tail-integral change of variable, and a dominating independent-subsequence bound establish the Gamma(4/3) coefficient. The code checks exact finite cyclic decomposition and numerical scaling without treating simulations as proofs.

The closest publicly indexed path symmetric-edge result determines inradius/center locus, not vertex-angle probabilities. D’Alì–Delucchi–Michałek establish tree-to-crosspolytope unimodular equivalence, which does not preserve the canonical Euclidean metric; Chen–Davis–Korchevskaia and Braun–Bruegge treat face/facet structure. value.rationale: The canonical Euclidean normal-cone measure of the terminal root is a natural geometric invariant of the path’s root polytope; the common crosspolytope face lattice gives no such metric information. The theorem identifies a nontrivial fractional-power and logarithmic boundary correction under deletion of one closing edge, with an exact positive constant from a rare adjacent extremal event. The effect is asymptotically larger than the combinatorial 1/n² change in vertex count, and it isolates a natural boundary phenomenon rather than computing an arbitrary low-dimensional sample.
